newsitem.title: UK: BA CEO aims to go ahead with job cuts - paper.
newsitem.headline: BA CEO aims to go ahead with job cuts - paper.

text.p: British Airways Plc needs to follow through with its efficiency measures despite the pain of the company's plan to cut 5,000 jobs, chief executive Robert Ayling said in a newspaper interview published on Monday.

"I do sincerely believe that unless we achieve an improvement in our competitiveness, the dangers we face will be far greater than the affects of the changes," Ayling was quoted as saying in the Independent.
BA unveiled the restructuring plan in September, saying it aimed to lop 1.0 billion pounds ($1.67 billion) off its annual cost base by the year 2000.
As part of the plan, BA said it would shed 5,000 of its 49,000 British staff.
Separately, British newspapers reported on Monday that BA had agreed with the Balpa pilots union on a set of principles aimed at improving their negotiating relationship.
The 10 points covered exchange of information, flexibility, and problem-solving, the Financial Times reported.
An industrial dispute last summer threatened to bring nearly all of BA's 3,500 flight crew out on strike.
BA recently unveiled a controversial alliance with AMR Corp's American Airlines, under which the two airlines would coordinate trans-atlantic flights.
